summary.text: 備 is interpreted as a person carrying an arrow container, a scene associated with being prepared. The simplified character 备 corresponds to 備; its pictured container’s original name and any sound match remain uncertain.

formation.text: 備 is analyzed as a phonosemantic compound: 人 depicts a person, and 𤰈 depicts arrows in a container while also being assigned a sound role. The carrying scene is linked with preparedness, but the pictured object’s original name and the proposed sound match are unverified. The 1956 scheme lists 备 as corresponding to 備.

components.text: In 備, 人 depicts the person in the proposed carrying scene associated with preparedness.
In 備, 𤰈 depicts arrows in a container, identified in texts as a quiver. It is also assigned a sound role, though the available comparison does not independently establish that role.

sound_limitation.text: The reported comparison does not independently establish 𤰈’s identity, reading, or phonetic role; the pictured object’s original name and any sound match to 箙 are also unresolved.

sound.text: The reported Zhengzhang forms share an initial and have similar rhymes, making a sound relationship plausible without verifying the analysis.

components.text: 备 is officially adopted as the simplified form corresponding to 備. A secondary account proposes a route through variant 俻, but the official scheme does not establish that derivation.

history.text: 備 is reported in oracle-bone, bronze, and manuscript script categories, but the earliest appearance is not dated in the available accounts.

The right-hand component is printed as 𤰇 in some forms and described as a change from seal-script 𤰈. Bronze forms also show its lower part changing to 用, tentatively proposed as a sound element. These descriptions do not establish a complete dated sequence.
The 1956 simplification scheme lists 备 as corresponding to 備. 俻 was separately recognized as a variant of 備, but the scheme does not identify it as the direct source of 备.

uncertainties.text: The proposed carrying-quiver interpretation links the graph with preparedness but does not establish the spoken word’s earliest meaning. Texts identify the pictured container as 箙, and 備 is reported writing 箙 in a bronze inscription; neither fact establishes the pictured object’s original name or proves a sound match to 𤰈.

Reported uses include prepared or complete, for use, cautious, equipment, and all or entirely. The cited examples do not establish a complete chronology or continuous development among these meanings.

senses.text: Bronze uses are reported with glosses such as “equipped” or “complete” and “for use.” The carrying-quiver scene may help explain preparedness, but does not prove the word’s earliest spoken sense.

senses.period: received lexicographic tradition; date of spoken sense unresolved
senses.text: The received dictionary gloss 慎也 means “cautious” or “careful”; it does not establish the earliest spoken meaning.
Dictionary citations include uses glossed “all” or “entirely,” but do not establish when this sense arose or how it relates chronologically to preparation or completeness.
Later cited examples use 備 for equipment or facilities. The evidence does not establish that this meaning followed a particular earlier sense.

limitations.text: The earliest attested spoken sense is unresolved. Reported bronze contexts and received dictionary glosses do not provide a complete dated history of the meanings.

A bronze inscription reportedly uses 備 as a written sign for 箙, “quiver,” a different word. This proposed phonetic borrowing would depend on similarity between the words’ pronunciations; the evidence here does not verify that resemblance or recover the pictured object’s original name or pronunciation.
